---
title: "quarto-index per-document state, index declarations"
# Smart typography is off for the reason every other probe turns it off: the
# marks below are compared byte for byte between two renders, and a rendered
# curly quote would be one more thing standing between the emitted output and
# the state that produced it.
from: markdown-smart
filters:
  - index
  - ../tests/state-pollute.lua
---

# What this fixture is for

This fixture declares no index, which is what makes the cells `indexes.lua`
owns readable. A document that declares one has its own declaration read over
whatever was left behind, so a leaked name, title or word would leave nothing
for the comparison to see. It is rendered twice off one tree, once with the
pollution filter above switched on and once with it off, and the two renders'
output and warnings must agree byte for byte.

# The marks

**A mark naming an index nothing declares.** [Named]{.index index="leaked"}
draws the report saying so and files in the one index this document has. A
leaked title table answers to that name instead, so both the report and the
entry move.

**A cross-reference**, so that the word printed in front of a target is on the
page: [Alpha]{.index see="Beta"} points at [Beta]{.index}.

**A term marked twice**, so that the mark printed between two locators is on
the page: [Twice]{.index} here, and [Twice]{.index} again here.

**A term that files under no letter**, so that the heading over that group is
on the page: [%percent]{.index}.

::: {.qi-index-here}
:::

Prose after the marker, so the index has something to sit in front of.
